records.topic: Exhortation to fight despite numerical disadvantage

candidates.difference: Gideon's troop reduction stresses divine victory and avoiding Israel's boasting, not the Qur'anic exhortation with twenty-to-two-hundred and hundred-to-thousand ratios.

records.question: Check Hebrew wording and the role of divine assistance; do not present numerical ratios as an earlier textual parallel.

records.topic: Modified numerical expectation and acknowledgment of weakness
records.question: Investigate legal/exegetical discussion of changed battle ratios; no sufficiently precise pre-Islamic parallel identified in this preliminary pass.

records.topic: Captives and worldly gain in the context of battle

candidates.difference: Deuteronomy sets rules for besieged cities and captives; the Qur'an addresses the prophet's taking captives before military subjugation and criticizes worldly gain.

records.question: Compare legal settings carefully; assess whether any specific pre-Islamic rule addresses ransom or captivity before victory.

records.topic: Warning of punishment absent a prior divine decree
records.question: Examine tafsir context and the preceding/following ayat before proposing any external parallel; no precise antecedent established.

records.topic: Permissibility of consuming lawful spoils with fear of God

candidates.difference: Numbers prescribes allocation and tribute from Midianite booty; the Qur'an permits lawful spoils and commands piety, without giving those allocation fractions here.
Deuteronomy allows taking certain spoils of war; its military setting and restrictions differ from the Qur'anic statement.

records.question: Check Hebrew text and source context; distinguish shared ancient war-spoils practice from literary borrowing.
